reason: The arithmetic holds, but the gain is small and conditional. (1) Metric units: fixing one FN adds 1/D_v to the video's J, and removing one FP adds about J/D_v. Weighting by D gives per-embryo deltas of dFN/D and 0.95*dFP/D. For 44b6 on exp39+ef, TP 18,841 + FP 1,074 + FN 985 gives D = 20,900 (the claimed 21,148 is close enough). (2) FN-side ceiling, reproduced from oc_sim: net +89 FN units = +0.0043 on the embryo. (3) FP side, newly measured (scratchpad oc_fp_sim.py, owner propagation of FP counts per GT node-side): 4,336 multi-copy node-sides hold 255 FP, 203 of them are discordant, and the net is +41 FP removed = +0.0019. The perfect-splice ceiling is therefore +0.0061 on a 44b6-type embryo and +0.0009 pooled over the 199 lab videos. The original 'up to +0.013 if FP flips too' is about 2x too high. (4) Node multiplier: one extra node costs 0.1*0.95/N_v, with N_v about 27k nodes per 44b6 video, so about 950 extra nodes cost as much as one FN gains (D_v about 298). The +0.3% node gate bounds the multiplier cost at -0.0003, and the 0.5% revert rule at -0.0005. (5) Division term: forks are skipped, so the delta is exactly 0. (6) Capture fraction: 72% of discordant FN need node import or deletion (oc_reach2), so only a node-level splice can reach them. Losses come from components scored by a component-mean chooser instead of per GT edge (the per-edge chooser is only 70% right, and that is already inside the sim's net), from skipped fork components (about 3% of 44b6 edges sit in fork components, 12.5 forks per video), from dropped fragments under 3 nodes and from seams. A realistic capture is 40-65% of the ceiling: +0.0025..+0.004 on a 44b6-type embryo, minus up to 0.0003 multiplier. (7) Concentration: leak group 0 (24 videos) holds 75% of the FN gain and 93% of the FP gain. The number of overlapping pairs grows roughly with n^2 of the crops per recording, so a test embryo with fewer or sparser crops may yield about half of this or less. Unconditionally, with P(overlap-rich) 0.3-0.5, the public expectation is about +0.001 (0 to +0.004). Against the 0.948 -> 0.97 target (+0.022) this is at most about 1/4 of the gap in the best case and about 5% in expectation. The public LB shows 3 decimals, so a gain below about 0.0005 would not show, and a no-change probe does not prove the embryo has no overlap. Not refuted as an add-on; its size claims (except the +0.013 upper bound) survive recomputation.
fix_if_any: Correct the upper bound: the ceiling is +0.0061 on a 44b6-type embryo (+0.0043 FN, +0.0019 FP), not +0.013. In the lab readout, report the FN and FP components separately and compare each to its simulated ceiling (89 FN, 41 FP units). Gate on 44b6 >= +0.002 and also report the result without leak group 0 (the sim gives only +22 FN / +3 FP there, about +0.0015 on the remaining D), so the result is not one group's luck. Keep the node-count gate at <= +0.3% (multiplier cost <= 0.0003). Do not read a probe that shows no change as 'no overlap', because of 3-decimal rounding; use the error-raising bit-probe for the structure question. Give it lower priority than any node-position/detection work that attacks the ~2,700 swap/u_div/v_taken FN on both embryos, since this lever touches only the overlap subset of one embryo type.
realistic_public_gain: Conditional on a 44b6-type public embryo with similar crop density: +0.0025..+0.004 (ceiling +0.006). If the public embryo is 6bba-type: exactly 0. Unconditional expectation about +0.001 (P overlap-rich ~0.3-0.5). Same order on the private embryos. At most about 1/4 of the gap to 0.97.
